system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Project Kestrel — buyer-side review

The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and assertion that provisions have been cleared do not establish Buyer acceptance. The positions below should be reviewed and negotiated against the agreed **AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free purchase of 100% of Paperbark Analytics**, under NSW law.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% of price: AUD 4.8m**. | A higher, commercially negotiated cap, with separate protection for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Reopen the cap; propose at least 30% (AUD 7.2m)** as a negotiating position. A 20% cap may leave material undisclosed business liabilities with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000** individually; aggregate qualifying claims must exceed **AUD 250,000**, with only the excess recoverable. | A lower de minimis and a **tipping basket**, under which the full amount is recoverable once the threshold is crossed; exclusions for fundamental claims, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket.** The Seller’s deductible basket transfers the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying loss to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranty claims must be notified within **18 months**; limitations apply to all claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with longer or separate periods for fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims. | **Seek 24 months and category-specific survival periods.** Eighteen months may expire before a full post-completion reporting and audit cycle reveals a problem. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and 18-month limit. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, authority, ownership and unencumbered title, with a cap up to **100% of price**, longer survival and no general thresholds. | **Reject the general regime for fundamental warranties.** Failure to acquire valid title to the whole company strikes at the core of the transaction. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to **all claims of any nature**; no express fraud exception is stated. | An express, effective carve-out for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation from caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, knowledge, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions. | **Insert an express fraud carve-out throughout the relevant clauses.** The all-claims language creates avoidable uncertainty over recourse for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | All data-room contents, accounts, registers and public records are generally disclosed, irrespective of the specific disclosures. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed**, in sufficient detail to identify nature and scope, against relevant warranties; a defined, indexed and fixed disclosure set. | **Delete blanket data-room and public-record disclosures; test each specific disclosure.** Mere availability of a document should not automatically qualify every warranty. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to the Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | No constructive or imputed knowledge bar; warranty qualification only through agreed fair disclosure, with an appropriate fraud carve-out. | **Delete the discoverability and adviser-knowledge bar.** It could defeat claims based on documents the Buyer had no meaningful opportunity to assess. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent condition treated as satisfied upon written consent. No final consent or evidence of satisfaction of associated conditions is included. Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6m / 30% of FY26 revenue**. | A completion condition requiring valid written consent on terms acceptable to the Buyer, with all conditions in clause 11.3 satisfied or validly waived and evidence delivered before completion. | **Make verified, unconditional consent a completion condition; strengthen Seller obligations to procure it.** A letter alone may not satisfy the contract’s conditions or protect a major customer relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release proposed after completion. No final discharge is included. | Completion repayment from Seller proceeds under an agreed funds flow, a lender payout statement, and simultaneous release/discharge or a binding completion undertaking with an enforceable release process. | **Do not complete on a mere post-completion release promise.** The debt-free/cash-free bargain requires the debt and security to be dealt with at completion. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses are said to be the Seller’s matter but are omitted from funds flow; on-costs are unknown. | Seller bears the bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, without leakage or double counting; funds flow or price adjustment expressly provides for payment or reimbursement. | **Quantify and allocate the full cost expressly before signing.** Conditional employee obligations may become a company expense at or after completion despite the Seller’s statement. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 open**, but does not independently prove non-payment. Transfer of SOW3 materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; no receipt or confirmatory assignment is present. | Evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment or other satisfactory confirmation of rights, plus an indemnity covering losses arising from deficient ownership or rights and related claims, costs and remediation. | **Require the documents and broaden the indemnity beyond the fee.** Paying an outstanding amount alone may not resolve ownership, third-party claims or business disruption. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material. A link went to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification obligations remain unknown. | Prompt investigation and preservation of evidence; assessment of access, affected records and applicable notification obligations; cooperation, remediation and a tailored indemnity or other agreed protection. | **Complete targeted diligence and negotiate incident-specific protection.** The incident is not a confirmed breach, but its scope and potential exposure remain unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** are ordinary-course costs. The disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. | Review DD-008 and DD-011 together; establish timing, scope, cancellation rights and accrual, then allocate any pre-completion or non-ordinary-course exposure through price mechanics or a specific protection. | **Verify before accepting the Seller’s classification.** The available facts do not establish whether these costs belong economically to the Seller or Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise; exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions also apply to all claims. | An express hierarchy and separate regimes for general and fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, price adjustments, debt repayment and fraud; avoid unintended overlap or double recovery. | **Rewrite the cross-cutting provisions and check every exception.** An “all claims” sweep can silently neutralise individually negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of **100%**; Seller relies on it as title evidence. | Independently verify the issued share capital, Seller’s ownership, encumbrances and transfer requirements against the register, constitution and relevant corporate records; obtain transfer documents and fundamental title warranties. | **Verify title and completion deliverables independently.** The register is useful evidence but alone does not establish all matters needed for an unencumbered transfer. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties are treated as settled under the general regime. | A dedicated pre-completion tax covenant/indemnity with an appropriate longer claims period and separate cap and thresholds; substantive IP ownership, licensing and infringement warranties, with a tailored regime and Ironquay protection. | **Reopen both categories and specify their survival and limitations.** General warranty protection may be inadequate for tax liabilities discovered later and IP risks central to an analytics business. |

**Priority before signing or completion:** resolve Bluefen’s consent conditions, Riverlark repayment and security release, the bonus allocation, and Ironquay rights; investigate the export incident and renewals. The proposed caps and periods above are Buyer negotiating positions, not assertions that the Seller has agreed to them.
=== END ADVICE ===
